Plim reveals a wheeled home robot with remote family participation

Devanthro becomes Plim Robotics and publishes a home-assistance concept and specifications, with price and delivery dates still undisclosed.

Humanoids Daily ↗17 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Assistance and remote presence

Devanthro has become Plim Robotics. Its proposed home robot combines AI assistance with remote operation, allowing relatives or caregivers to appear on its face display and interact through its body. The company advertises operation across distances up to 9,000 km.

Published specifications

Plim is listed at 1.65 m and 80 kg, with an omnidirectional wheeled base, seven-degree-of-freedom arms rated for 3 kg, and two-finger grippers. Jetson Thor and ROS 2 support the system; battery runtime is two hours with automatic docking.

Performance remains unquantified

Families and care organizations can register interest, but pricing, delivery dates and household task-success rates remain undisclosed. Two hours of battery life does not imply all-day operation without charging, and the frequency of human intervention is unknown.
